title: Investigate and fix connection stall during multipath failover (hosted -> dedicated path flapping)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Multiple customers reported elevated 5xxs and long tail connection stalls during tenant failovers between hosted and dedicated pools. Root behavior: when multipath routing flips an in-flight streaming/long-poll request from hosted->dedicated, the edge proxy sometimes leaves a half-open session; the client SDK retries, creating duplicate in-flight streams that contend for the same KV cache entries and cause cascading timeouts downstream. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and a staged rollforward.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a test tenant routed to hosted pool A with multipath enabled
2) Start a high-rate batch of streaming requests that hold KV-cache handles (simulated long prompt + streaming tokens)
3) Trigger routing flip to dedicated pool by toggling routing weight in the test control plane
4) Observe edge proxy logs for partially closed TLS sessions, client-side retries, and repeated idempotency tokens
5) Correlate with runtime traces: KV cache eviction spikes + increased per-token latencies -> 502/504s
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between 'stream:half_open' events at edge and tenant-level retry bursts in Grafana dashboard (grafana.redwood/team/multipath)
Edge code path occasionally returns a 200 with empty body during failover; SDK treats that as success for non-streaming but streaming callers initiate reconnects -> duplication
KV cache hot-key contention reproduces locally when two streams use same conversation ID and identical idempotency token; cache lock is coarse-grained for streaming endpoints
Dedicated pool warmup added latency; probe pings were insufficient to prevent early client retries
Customer-supplied traces (cust: AcmeHealth) show idempotency-token reuse due to SDK BACKOFF bug (SDK-1023) amplifying duplicate in-flight requests
decision_notes: Short term: implement edge fast-abort for duplicate in-flight idempotency tokens (hotfix) to prevent KV contention and reduce 5xx blast radius
Medium term: add streaming-lease semantics in runtime that serialize exclusive KV access per conversation id and degrade to read-only mode during failover
Long term: update SDK to guarantee unique streaming idempotency tokens and add client-level jittered backoff guidance in docs
We will roll hotfix to canary region (us-west-2) behind feature flag and run synthetic load for 6 hours before wider rollout
acceptance_criteria: No repeat 5xx waves in canary over 6h synthetic run under simulated failover
Edge metrics: 'stream:half_open' events reduced by >= 90% during failover window
KV cache eviction rate returns to baseline within two minutes of failover
Positive signoff from on-call and customer success for two impacted customers (AcmeHealth, ShopFast)
action_items: A) Implement edge fast-abort for duplicate active idempotency tokens - PR: github.com/redwood/release/PR-1209
B) Add a streaming-lease lock in runtime to prevent concurrent exclusive KV writes - branch: runtime/stream-lease
C) Patch SDK to jitter and generate streaming-specific idempotency tokens - ticket SDK-1023
D) Add a Grafana panel and alert for 'stream:half_open' > 5/min - dashboard/grafana/tiles/stream_failover.json
E) Run customer canary with AcmeHealth test harness and collect traces via tracing-s3-bucket: s3://rwd-traces/2025-02-19-acme

resolution_summary: Hotfix (PR-1209) introduced an edge-level fast-abort for duplicate active streaming idempotency tokens which prevented duplicate in-flight streams during multipath failover. Canary results show significant reduction in KV contention and 5xx waves. Follow-ups: implement streaming-lease in runtime, fix SDK jitter/backoff, and create customer-facing guidance. Postmortem and retrospective scheduled in Confluence.
